::: {.tut-standfirst}
Step-by-step guides to take your occurrence spreadsheet from the field notebook to a Darwin Core Archive — following the same workflow as the application, step by step.
:::

The tutorials follow the Saíra workflow, step by step. Use the **sidebar** on the left to move between them and the **previous / next** buttons at the bottom of each page — the reading flows continuously, from installation to the final export. Each step can also be read on its own.

## The workflow, from raw data to DwC-A

1. **[Installation and first steps](01-installation.qmd)** — install Saíra from GitHub and open the application in your browser.
2. **[Importing your data](02-upload.qmd)** — load CSV or Excel spreadsheets and run a first inspection of the columns.
3. **[Mapping fields to Darwin Core](03-dwc-mapping.qmd)** — match each column to a Darwin Core term with automatic suggestions.
4. **[Validating scientific names](04-name-validation.qmd)** — check the nomenclature, resolve synonyms and standardize spelling.
5. **[Validating coordinates](05-coordinate-validation.qmd)** — find missing or swapped coordinates and review them on the map.
6. **[Preview and export](06-preview-export.qmd)** — review the result, handle sensitive species and generate the Darwin Core Archive.

::: {.callout-note}
## The workflow is flexible
You don't have to follow every step in a rigid sequence. Saíra lets you go back to any step — remap a field, reload the spreadsheet or revalidate — without losing the work you've already done.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Practice with the sample file
Download the sample spreadsheet [`ocorrencias-exemplo.csv`](../../assets/exemplo/ocorrencias-exemplo.csv) and follow the tutorials with it. It is a small, deliberately imperfect dataset (with a problematic accent and a swapped coordinate), ideal for practicing validation.
:::
